findings:
🟠 [setsid-wait-sid-picks-grandchild] MUST-FIX On the `setsid --wait` (HAVE_SETSID=1, non-detached) path the WORKER_SID capture targets the wrong process. util-linux `setsid` only forks when the caller is already a process-group leader; a `cmd &` child of a non-job-control bash is not a leader, so `setsid --wait env ...` execs in place and `$rp` IS the worker (session leader, sid=pgid=rp). `_setsid_wait_worker_sid` then deliberately polls up to ~1s for a child of `$rp` and returns the first *grandchild* pid (e.g. the worker's own `sleep`/`git`/helper). In `_watchdog_signal_worker`, `kill -SIG -<grandchild>` fails with ESRCH (no pgrp has that id) and the fallback `kill -SIG <grandchild>` signals a single grandchild, not the worker tree — violating the spec's "signal the worker's own process group or session". Impact: a real worker (node CLI) that spawns a short-lived child at poll time gets WORKER_SID=<already-exited pid>, both TERM and KILL hit nothing, `wait $rp` blocks unbounded and the run reports `timeout_enforced:true` while unenforced; a worker that supervises its child survives the child kill. The test only passes because the stub's `sleep` is its sole child and the stub exits 0 once sleep dies (a `while :; do sleep 1; done` stub would hang the suite). Evidence that this host is in the no-fork regime: the detached test passes with `WORKER_SID=$rp` from `setsid env ... &` — if setsid had forked there, the non-`--wait` parent would have exited immediately and `wait $rp` would return before the deadline. Smallest fix: in `_setsid_wait_worker_sid`, poll bounded (same 20×50ms) for EITHER `ps -o sid= -p "$rp"` == `$rp` (no fork → return `$rp`) OR a child `c` of `$rp` with `ps -o sid= -p "$c"` == `$c` (fork → return `$c`); never return a pid whose sid≠pid; fall back to `$rp`. Alternative: launch with `setsid --fork --wait` so the leader is always exactly the single child of `$rp`. Add a loop-stub (`trap '' TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done`) case on the forced-setsid path so group-kill is actually discriminated.
🔵 [setsid-nowait-fork-exit-hazard] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Plain/detached-child paths use bare `setsid env ... &` and assume no fork; if the dispatcher ever runs with job control on (or a caller wraps it so bg children become pgrp leaders), setsid forks and its parent exits immediately, so `wait $rp` returns 0 instantly and the worker runs orphaned. Excluded because the diff never enables `set -m` on these branches and current evidence shows no-fork; hardening (`setsid --wait` when supported, or verifying `ps -o sid= -p $rp` == `$rp` before the wait) is a follow-up.
🔵 [timed-out-on-deadline-coincident-exit] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `.fired` is created before TERM is sent; a worker that exits on its own in the same instant is reported `timed_out:true`/`status:failure` although the watchdog did not terminate it. Excluded as a sub-second race with harmless outcome; a follow-up could record AGENT_EXIT/`wait` status ordering to disambiguate.
🔵 [test-global-pgrep-flakiness] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `assert_r1_no_stray_watchdog` uses `pgrep -f 'hetero-wall-watchdog'` host-wide and `assert_timeout_kill_result` requires <12s wall including worktree setup, both fragile under parallel CI or slow hosts. Excluded: test-only, not product behavior; scope pgrep to the run's `hetero-wdog-tok-*` tag and widen the elapsed bound if flaky.
